requirements: Read the R4 receipt and archived fresh repetition XML/logs (SHA-256 cadf6049c961067d5a5b56b9cd701c22574d0271daee8ce8264e0e791a33ebe0). Do not reuse stale XML or infer a pass from an unobserved failure.

Identify which loop iteration/transport and which endpoint was in use; capture server and client connection lifecycle, request and handler entry counts, response status and headers actually sent or received, teardown/order, timing and full exception chains. Preserve fresh logs and XML. Use narrowly scoped disposable instrumentation if necessary and preserve the exact patch, separate results from unmodified-head runs, and disclose any changed timing.

Trace the endpoint fixture, JDK and Jetty clients and underlying lifecycle to distinguish fixture races, real client defects and host/environment problems. Test the leading hypothesis with a discriminating experiment or control; propose a concrete minimal correction with its rationale and limitations. Do not weaken the forged-marker assertion, add retries merely to mask failure, or claim replay occurred when the assertion was not reached.

Report exact observations, recurrence and confidence, evidence location and SHA-256, environment, commands and complete exit codes. Use passed only if diagnosis is supported by discriminating evidence; otherwise failed, incomplete or non-reproduced as appropriate. A diagnostic receipt is not a full production gate. Publish receipt before canonical release including executor-stop, process and host-lock evidence.
